newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end softer, but avoid Dow selloff.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end softer, but avoid Dow selloff.

* Toronto stocks ended softer on Wednesday, but avoided New York's sell off * Weak golds, merchandising offset by gains in media, energy * 112 million shares traded worth C$1.93 billion
Toronto stocks ended softer on Wednesday, but media and energy stocks helped the Canadian market avoid New York's steep decline.

The TSE 300 Composite Index dropped 16.89 points to close at 5929.98 in brisk turnover of 112.6 million shares worth C$1.93 billion. On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average sank 51 points to close around 6549.
Despite weakness in golds, merchandising and transportation, "there was fair amount of strength in the (Toronto) market," said Jim Doak, director of investment research for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
The gold sector dropped 267 points as Comex February gold closed down US$2.90 an ounce at US$356.80 after hitting lows around US$355.30 an ounce.
The transport and merchandising groups also lost ground due to sell-offs in individual stocks. The strong side was led by communications, oil and gas, and real estate.
Declining stocks outnumbered advances 500 to 486 with 257 issues unchanged.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Loewen Group Inc sank after rival Service Corp International dropped its US$2.9 billion takeover bid.
Loewen's stock dropped 5.95 to 49.75 on 3.8 million shares and depressed the TSE's merchandising group. Loewen had hit a high of 58.75 during its takeover fight with Service Corp.
* Among weak golds, Barrick Gold Corp fell 1 to 35.55, while Placer Dome Inc slipped 0.55 to 27.05.

* Laidlaw Inc class B dropped 0.60 to 17.40 on 4.3 million shares after soaring to new heights on Tuesday. Investors rushed to buy Laidlaw's stock after the company announced two major deals worth over US$2 billion late Monday.
* The top gaining energy stock was Dreco Energy class A which closed up 2.25 to 53.75. Gulf Canada added 0.40 to 10.70.
